The instant appeal has been preferred against the Judgment and Award dated 25th August, 2023 passed by the learned Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, 1st Court,
Nadia, in MAC Case no. 221 of 2015.

sentences.text:
The brief facts of the case is that the appellants being the claimants have preferred an application under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, before the learned tribunal for getting compensation on the ground that their predecessor was died in a road traffic accident due to rash and negligent driving of Raju Sk. & Ors vs National Insurance Co. 1 the driver of the offending vehicle duly insured under the policy of the Insurance Company.

sentences.text: The claim case was contested by the Insurance Company.
After hearing the parties and after receiving the evidences the learned tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.5,90,000/- in favour of the claimants.
Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the above award, the present appeal has been preferred by the claimants.
Learned advocate for the appellants submits that the award passed by the learned tribunal is erroneous.
The learned tribunal has wrongly assessed the income of the deceased to be Rs.4,000/-per month.
The deceased was a Van Rickshaw Puller and he used to earn Rs. 6,000/- per month.
The PW-1 has deposed to that effect that the victim used to earn Rs. 6,000/- per month.
The evidence made by the claimants before the learned tribunal was not considered.
So, the award passed by the learned tribunal is not just and proper compensation.
So, he prayed for necessary enhancement.

Ms. Paul, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the Insurance Company raised strong objection and submits that the learned tribunal has considered the all materials before him but there were no relevant documents of income.

But, on considering the submission of the claimants, the learned tribunal has fixed the monthly income of the deceased Rs. 4,000/- instead of notional income of Rs.
3,000/-.
The learned tribunal has awarded the compensation observing the guideline of the Hon'ble Apex Court passed in Pranay Sethi.
So, at this juncture, the award passed by the learned tribunal cannot be altered or modified.
Heard the learned advocates perused the materials on record.
It appears that the monthly income of the deceased is only the relevant points to be considered by the appellate Court.
It was pleaded by the claimant that the monthly income of the deceased was Rs. 6,000/-.
No documentary evidences were produced the deceased was a Van Rickshaw Pullers in that score, it is true that no documentary evidence shall be available regarding such occupation.

Considering the fact that the learned tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased to be Rs.
4,000/-.
I find no infirmity in the observation passed by the learned tribunal.

However, this Court has adopted a view on several occasions that when a person died in a road traffic accident in the year 2015 onwards, the notional income should be considered to be Rs. 5,000/- per month; the same view may be adopted in this case.
Accordingly, the income of the deceased shall be considered to be Rs. 5,000/- per month.

Considering the same award passed by the learned tribunal need be modified as hereunder:-
Calculation of compensation 1.

Monthly Income :Rs.5,000/-

sentences.text:
Add: 25% Future Prospects :Rs.1,250/-
: Rs.6,250/-
3.

Annual Income (Rs. 6,250 X 12) :Rs.75,000/-
4. Multiplier 13 (Rs.75,000 X 13) :Rs.9,75,000/-

5 . Less: 1/3rd for personal Exp. :Rs.3,25,000/-
:Rs.6,50,000/-
6.
Add: General Damages :Rs.77,000/- Total Compensation :Rs. 7,27,000/- Less: Already received :Rs. 5,90,000/- Enhance compensation :Rs.1,37,000/-
After calculation it appears that the just and proper compensation comes to Rs.7,27,000/-.
The claimants have already received the award amounting to Rs.5,90,000/-.
The balance enhance compensation comes to Rs.1,37,000/-.
The balance award shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim application till the deposit of the earlier award by the Insurance Company before the learned tribunal.

The Insurance Company is directed to pay the compensation through the office of the learned Registrar General High Court Calcutta by providing three equal account payee cheques in the name of the appellants herein within eight weeks.

On such deposit the claimants are at liberty to receive the cheque from the office of the learned Registrar General, High Court, Calcutta according to the prevalent Rules of identification and satisfaction through the learned advocate.
The received of the compensation by the appellants/claimants is subject to the payment of deficit Court Fees to be paid before the learned tribunal.
The learned tribunal shall act upon the certified copy of this order regarding receiving of the deficit Court Fees.
The instant FMAT (MV) 813 of 2023 is disposed of.
All connected pending applications, if any, stand disposed of.
Interim orders, if any, stand vacated.
Parties to act upon the server copy and urgent certified copy of this order be provided on usual terms and conditions.

(Subhendu Samanta, J.)
